layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Odyssey of the Mind (OM) promotes creativity, problem solving, teamwork, and more. It is a creative

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: problem-solving competition that gives kids the confidence to think for themselves and to create solutions to any

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: challenge. Independent study, original ideas, and critical thinking skills are rewarded over getting the “one right

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: answer" thanks to our unique open-ended problems that are backed by educators and experts in STE(A)M fields.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Performance, art & cultural studies are also incorporated, creating a well-rounded program that has impacted lives

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for over 40 years. OM benefits all types of students as they learn to think outside the box.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Participation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Students work in teams of up to seven members and spend weeks or months working together and creating

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solutions to long-term problems. Every year, there are six long-term problems designed for them to choose from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Teams are formed by division and compete against teams in the same division and problem. Grade level

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: determines the division for teams.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • In the competition, teams have eight minutes to present their long-term problem solution. They will be scored for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: how well they meet the requirements of the problem (Long-Term score) and for their creativity in categories

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: specific to that problem (Style score).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Cost

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Yearly memberships are required to participate in OM. Each membership supports one team per problem per

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: division.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Standard Membership $290: Individual schools/ Multiple schools sharing a principal.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Additional Membership $190: Only for schools who enter two teams in the same problem and division in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: competition.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Awards

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 第3页/共12页

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Ranatra Fusca Creativity Award: It represents the essence of OM. It is presented to teams or individuals who

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: exhibit exceptional creativity, either through some aspect of their problem solution, or an extraordinary idea beyond

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the problem solution.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • OMER's Award: It recognizes individuals or teams who demonstrate outstanding sportsmanship, excellent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: behavior, or exceptional talent.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Odyssey of the Mind Creativity Award: It recognizes an individual and/ or organization for extraordinary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: creative achievement or exceptional effort.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Odyssey of the Mind Spirit Award: It recognizes an individual involved in the program who demonstrates the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: encouragement and development of cooperation, self-respect, and the appreciation and understanding of others.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: I've always been a daring risk taker. But when I was 15, my luck ran out. A horseback riding accident resulted

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in severe injuries, the death of my beloved horse Spooks, and the horrible news that I'd never ride again. I was set

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on proving the doctors wrong. Just a few months later, with my mother's support, I rode sidesaddle and won my

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: first jumping competition. The excitement was incredible.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sidesaddle

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: From then on, I committed my life to adventure, remembering my mother's lesson:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: never say, “I can't". At 22, I read about an opening to be a motorcycle trick rider — I'd

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learned to ride a few years earlier. Still, it was 1976 and I knew they were unlikely to hire a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: woman. I thought about that as I signed my trick rider application, leaving off the honorific

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: — Ms., hoping to hide the fact that I was a woman. But they never got back to me.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: I was heartbroken. Maybe the position had already been filled; maybe they'd discovered I was a woman. My

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: friend Steve then proposed an idea that at first seemed crazy: learning to fly aeroplanes. “Flying is for men," I

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: laughed at the idea. But gradually, I realized the suggestion had stuck with me.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Years ago, trial flights — brief introductory sessions with an instructor — cost just £5 for 15 minutes in the air

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Steve and I both signed up, and after my first session, I couldn't stop talking about flying. I got my license and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: headed for the US to work as a pilot. It wasn't easy. Initially, people were doubtful about a woman working in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: role, but I ended up outperforming my male colleagues. Twenty years later, I returned to England and started my

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: own flying company.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 第4页/共12页

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Now, I live a quieter life. I’ve settled in a village in Lincolnshire, spending much of my time volunteering in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: care homes. Last October, after nearly fifty years and countless adventures, I received a letter from a post office in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Staines. It was my trick rider application. The post office apologized for the delay and explained it had been found

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stuck behind a drawer in the office — the company never received it.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Looking back, I realized that even though I didn't get that job, it led me to a series of adventures that shaped

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: my life in unexpected and fulfilling ways.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Elephants and gorillas in the Republic of the Congo's rainforests spend a lot of time hiding in the shadows —

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or so we thought. Using drone (无人机) surveys and AI processing, scientists have discovered an extensive network

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of mysterious open clearings among the trees. Animals like elephants, gorillas visit these muddy areas, called bais,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the languages of the Indigenous Ba’Aka, to search for vital nutrition and maintain their complex social networks.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The numerous playgrounds are visible in satellite images, and AI analysis is helping researchers find them more

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effectively.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The discovery began in 2021 when Sylvain Ngouma and Evan Hockridge came upon a massive clearing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: during fieldwork in Odzala-Kokoua National Park and found a trail (踪迹) of wet, pot-sized footprints leading

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: through the woods to the open roundabout. Hockridge, who had thought bais were abnormal, says, “I had it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: backward. It kind of hit me when I was there. You can't understand animal interactions without first understanding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bais."

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For the next three summers, the team investigated the clearings. They analyzed camera-trap images,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: confirming what local people had told them — that these natural clearings are crucial gathering grounds for some

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the world's most endangered mammals. The bais, they realized, are big melting pots, big playgrounds, for a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: collection of forest animals.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 第5页/共12页

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: During the initial surveys, the team followed elephant trails to move through the rainforest from bai to bai.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This process led Hockridge to wonder about a network. Although previous studies documented animal behavior in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: selected bais, no one had counted them or had the means to map their distribution. The team partnered with African

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Parks, using drones to scan known sites. They trained an AI algorithm (算法) to identify bais in satellite imagery,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: revealing 2,176 clearings in one park — 10 times more than previously recorded.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Bais are always near rivers or streams. Most are smaller than a city block, but few, at more than 100 acres, are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bigger than some college campuses. “Bais are ultimately islands of resources, and animals produce these networks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of trails to essentially navigate to and from a network of bais," Hockridge says. The researchers' map of bais, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: first of its kind, is also a map of conservation priorities. “We find that a huge portion of the animal community

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: depends on this unique ecosystem. These species don't have alternative habitats other than bais," Hockridge says.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The study is also a step toward solving the ultimate mystery: How did bais form? Many ecologists have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: argued that a combination of hydrology (水文学) and animal landscaping is at play. But definitive proof remains

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: elusive. Now, with a map in hand and camera traps still in place, the research team is tracking long-term changes,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which have implications for the maintenance of these crucial animal habitats.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: “We have hypotheses (假说),"Andrew Davies, an ecologist in Harvard, says, "but the short answer is: we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: don't know."

layout_dets.text: Monday was the first day of Dartmouth's spring term. So, as I often do at this time, I started teaching my

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: course for non-science majors called “Understanding the Universe: From Atoms to the Big Bang".

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This is what students like to call a “physics for poets" class — a class that explores the history of how

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: humanity has faced some of the deepest questions we can ask about the material world and our place in it, without

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the math. It is a class that tries to capture the true spirit of the liberal-arts education, mixing the sciences and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: humanities as different and complementary ways of knowing the world and why we matter. In fancier words, as an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 第6页/共12页

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intellectual history of physics and astronomy (天文学), the class requires that scientific thinking be contextualized

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: culturally, so that students can situate the ways in which some of the most revolutionary ideas in the past 2,000

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: years emerged when they did.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Scientists, by training, have little exposure to the humanities. Given that a major in the sciences requires a lot

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of technical work, we spend precious little time dealing with what happened culturally and historically around the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: science we are trying to understand. This, I believe, is the reason why so many scientists in the public media

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: condemn (遣责) the humanities as useless. As a consequence, many scientific ideas are presented as having

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: addressed some of the deepest questions we have been asking, when they haven't.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Humanities students, on the other hand, are typically those who avoid the sciences or, at least, math. Their

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training is also technical, involving lots of reading and critical writing. You can often tell, when you teach this kind

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of class, who the scientists and the humanists are. All you have to do is write an equation (方程) on the blackboard

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and look at the class. Humanists will quickly look bored. The scientists will become lively. As you read from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Aristotle's Metaphysics, the opposite will happen. To bridge this gap is the challenge.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The classroom is the ideal place for this conversation between the sciences and the humanities to unfold. By

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: exposing students to the two sides of the cultural divide, we stand a chance of creating something that will actually

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: close the gap. Scientists should recognize that some research topics — AI, biotechnology, climate change, life

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: extension, nature, and many others — need to be investigated together with humanists as a joint effort.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: I finished the first class by reminding the students that not even the best teacher in the world can teach

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: someone who doesn't want to learn. After all, as Tom Stoppard reminded us in his brilliant play Arcadia, it is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: wanting to know that makes us matter — scientists and humanists alike.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: First, let's define forgiveness.25It's not about forgetting what happened or excusing harmful

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: choosing not to let that pain continue to define your thoughts, emotions, and behaviors.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Forgiveness is essential because we're all human, and we all make mistakes. If we want to cultivate
